Indifference

in-DIF-ur-uns -- stress on the second syllable, DIF. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Indifference is a lack of interest or concern.

What hurt most was not the argument but her indifference afterward, as though the whole thing had never mattered.

Worked Example

A club posts sign-up sheets for the biggest event of its year. A week later there are two names on the list, and neither person turns up to the meeting.

The response is indifference: not hostility, not enthusiasm, simply an absence of interest or concern. Indifference is the flat middle -- nobody objected, and nobody cared.

How Indifference Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

apathy

apathy: a total absence of interest or feeling

unconcern

unconcern: a lack of worry or care about something

detachment

detachment: emotional distance from what is happening

Antonyms

enthusiasm

enthusiasm: eager interest and excitement

concern

concern: care and worry about something

How Strong Is It? — unconcern → indifference → apathy

unconcern vs. indifference

unconcern vs. indifference: Unconcern is the mildest of the three -- a shrug of unconcern says one thing does not worry you -- while indifference says the whole matter fails to interest you at all.

apathy vs. indifference

apathy vs. indifference: Apathy spreads wider than indifference: indifference is aimed at one particular thing you do not care about, while apathy is a settled condition in which nothing stirs any feeling whatsoever.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of indifference.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin in-)

root — difference

root — difference: a way in which things are unlike (Latin differre 'to carry apart, to be unlike')

Put it together

Put it together: Indifference is this unit's prefix in- ('not') plus difference, a complete English word -- and the literal reading is startlingly exact: if you are indifferent, the outcomes make no difference to you. Win or lose, Tuesday or Wednesday, it is all the same, so you feel nothing about any of it.

Use the root in a new word: differentiate

Use the root in a new word: differentiate: Chemists differentiate the two compounds by their melting points.

Root Check

Word Choice

Indifference is the noun; the adjective is indifferent ('she was indifferent to the result'). Watch the preposition -- indifference to or toward something. Because the word marks the absence of feeling rather than bad feeling, it often stings more than anger does: the famous line is that the opposite of love is not hate but indifference.
